subject: Post-call recap: LuminaHealth evaluation decomposition & acceptance slate
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: LuminaHealth evaluation decomposition & acceptance slate

Hi Aisha — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a proposed, compact acceptance slate we can use to run the 4-week evaluation you asked for. I tried to keep this focused on measurable gates so your engineering and procurement teams can sign off quickly.

High-level objective:
- Prove that Redwood can serve the LuminaHealth assistant workload at production latency and cost targets without regressions in extraction quality.

Acceptance slate (proposed, numeric):
1) Latency: p95 generation <= 450 ms for typical 256-token requests (baseline input distribution you described).
2) Throughput: sustain 75 concurrent requests/sec for sustained 10-minute windows with tail isolation (no request queueing > 1s).
3) Cost efficiency: average effective cost <= $0.0035 per token at configured batching profile (we will propose batching settings to hit this).
4) Quality (content extraction use case): F1 for entity extraction >= 0.85 on your labeled eval set; hallucination rate <= 1% (measured via the provided checks).
5) Reliability: end-to-end availability >= 99.5% during the trial window; automatic fallback to a smaller model if p95 latency exceeds threshold for >3 consecutive minutes.

Owners (Redwood / Lumina):
- Redwood AE / coordination: Camila Reyes (me) — program lead and escalation owner.
- Redwood TSM / engineering contact: Ben Carter — performance tuning, test harness, and instrumentation.
- Redwood CS: Monica Patel — onboarding, data ingestion, and quality checks.
- Lumina technical lead: Aisha Khan — will provide sample payloads, eval labels, and redaction requirements.

Proposed 4-week cadence (compact):
- Week 0 (kickoff): share sample payloads, redaction rules, and one representative labeled eval slice (<= 500 records). Define final acceptance slate and test harness endpoints.
- Week 1: ingest sample payloads into a sandbox, baseline smoke runs, identify hotpaths and token distributions.
- Week 2: performance tuning (batching, quantization suggestion), run sustained throughput tests, collect p95/p99 profiles.
- Week 3: run labeled eval for quality gates, execute stability soak test, and finalize cost measurement.
- Week 4: readout with Lumina + handoff doc; rollback/failover plan if gates not met.

Immediate asks for Lumina (if you can):
- Provide one redacted eval slice (<= 500 rows) and a 1-hour representative production trace or synthetic workload to approximate arrival rates.
- Confirm any hard constraints (e.g., max latency allowed for interactive flows, PHI handling notes).

Attachments: I attached a one-page acceptance slate and a small sample payload template (redacted) for your review.

If that looks good we can lock the kickoff for next Tuesday and I’ll loop in engineering for a 30-min tech sync.

Thanks — Camila
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.ai

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@luminahealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: LuminaHealth evaluation decomposition & acceptance slate

Camila, thanks for the clear recap — this is exactly the kind of slate we need to evaluate quickly. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The F1 target looks reasonable; we may ask for minor relaxations on non-critical entity types, but will flag that in the eval slice.
- PHI/data handling: we can provide a redacted slice, but we need confirmation that logs and any persisted artifacts during the trial will be encrypted and retained for no more than 30 days. Please confirm Redwood’s retention defaults for trial sandboxes.
- Cost target: our procurement team would be comfortable with up to $0.004/token during the POC ramp if you can commit to the $0.0035/token target by the readout with the final configuration. Is that acceptable?

I’ll have our data engineer (cc’d in a separate note) push the labeled slice and a short synthetic trace file. We may also include a small set of failing examples to make sure hallucination checks are meaningful.

A couple of quick asks for your team before kickoff:
- A brief description of the harness endpoints we’ll call (auth, ingest, eval endpoints) so we can sanity-check with security.
- Confirmation on the retention/purge timeline for logs and cached KV.

If you can confirm those items I’ll lock resources on our side and confirm next Tuesday for kickoff.

— Aisha
Director, Product — LuminaHealth
aisha.khan@luminahealth.com

Adding a few technical specifics we should include in the acceptance doc and the harness so there is no ambiguity when we run automated checks: 

1) Latency measurement details:
- Use p95 and p99 measured end-to-end from client submit to final token received (not just inference kernel). Include time-to-first-byte (TTFB) for interactive flows.
- Baseline tokenization assumptions: typical prompt size = 120 input tokens, expected generation = 256 tokens. Provide a suggested harness payload with those params (attached).

2) Throughput/soak conditions:
- Sustained throughput target: 75 req/sec for 10-minute windows, plus 3 x 1-minute spike windows at 250 req/sec to test transient behavior.
- Track queueing time; any queueing delta > 1s counts as a violation.

3) Cost calculus:
- We’ll capture per-call token counts and compute effective cost = (model_cost_tokens + infra_amortized)/generated_tokens. We’ll instrument to report median and 95% cost per token.

4) Quality checks and tooling:
- Provide a small eval harness that runs the labeled slice, computes F1 and exact-match for critical entities, and measures hallucination by checking against a ground-truth pass/fail script.
- Suggest adding a lightweight human spot-check (10 examples) during week 3 to validate automated metrics.

5) Test harness ops expectations:
- We will host the harness scripts in a shared Drive link and provide a read-only service account token for Lumina to hit a sandbox endpoint.

Attachments included (drafts): eval_harness_instructions.md, synthetic_workload_template.jsonl

Also: Monica, can you confirm CS-side responsibilities for labeling support and weekly quality readouts? I’ll get engineering to stand by for the week 1-2 perf runs.

Ben
Technical Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Aisha — thanks for the quick turnaround. Confirming items below so we can lock kickoff: 

- Retention: Redwood trial sandboxes retain logs and caches for 30 days by default for POC sandboxes; we will enable AES-256 encryption at rest and in transit. We will share the retention and KMS details in the security packet at kickoff.
- Cost flex: we can accept $0.004/token as a ramp cap for the trial with a commitment to hit <= $0.0035/token by the final readout through batching + quantization where appropriate. We will document the configuration that achieves that target.

Next steps (what we’ll do this week):
1) I’ll post the acceptance sheet, harness instructions, and sample payloads to the Drive folder (link below).
2) Ben will share the synthetic workload template and a short smoke harness by tomorrow EOD.
3) Aisha will share the redacted eval slice + synthetic trace by Tuesday 12:00pm PT.
4) Schedule: Kickoff call Tuesday 2027-06-01 10:00am PT (30 min) — I’ll send an invite once you confirm.

If that schedule works I’ll mark resources and Ben will schedule 60-min windows for week 2 perf runs. Monica will run the quality readout cadence and own the week 3 human spot-check.
